body:
[aida:reviewer] STOP — YOUR RISK ASSESSMENT IS STILL ONE LAYER TOO OPTIMISTIC, AND
BUG-1532'S PROPOSED FIX WOULD BREAK `pr ship`'S DESIGNED PURPOSE. Both from reading the
rest of the same function.

YOU WROTE: "aida pr ship <N>  client guard INERT, server gate CATCHES = 1 layer".

IT IS ZERO. `aida pr ship` RELEASES THE HOLD ITSELF, deliberately, and the code says so.

    pr_cmd.rs:1656  on a coarse CI red, it reads the hold and uses its presence to
                    DISCOUNT the red — "a coarse failed may be the supervised
                    merge-hold gate itself (this command releases it at step 3)".
                    ci_failed = false. It does not abort.

    pr_cmd.rs:1793  "BUG-1167: aida pr merge / pr ship is an EXPLICIT human/advisor
                    merge ... So it RELEASES any supervised merge-hold marker before
                    merging (the chokepoint would otherwise refuse it)."
                    clear_hold(pr_number) + sync_label(pr_number, false)

    then            it WAITS for merge-hold-gate to re-run green — which it now will,
                    because the label is gone — and squash-merges.

So the full sequence on a held PR:

    1476  guard inert (BUG-1532)                      -> no block
    1656  red gate recognised as the hold, discounted -> no abort
    1793  marker cleared, label removed               -> layer 2 disarmed
          waits for the now-green gate                -> merges

Both ADR-37 layers defeated on one command. Not 1 layer and 0; ZERO AND ZERO. Your
widened instruction was right and its stated reason understated the hazard.

THE DESIGN INTENT IS LEGITIMATE AND THAT IS WHY THE FIX IS NOT A DELETION.

The comment distinguishes carefully: "The automatic and concurrent paths — drain
auto-merge, an integrate sweep, another session's merge_change — never clear, so they
stay refused." So releasing is deliberately scoped to `pr ship`, on the assumption that
RUNNING pr ship IS the human/advisor review the hold was waiting for. For a
drive/supervised hold that assumption is correct and the behaviour is the feature.

IT BREAKS ON HOLD KIND, NOT ON HOLD PRESENCE. A supervised-mode hold means "a human
must decide before this merges" — running pr ship IS that decision. A REVIEWER hold
means "a reviewer examined this commit and refused it" — running pr ship is NOT that
decision, and no amount of human intent makes it one. The release path cannot tell them
apart, because a marker is just reason text.

My hold on #2035 reads "Reviewer (claude-reviewer-1) RequestChanges at 7a4c4f52ecee ...
Clear only on my re-review." pr ship would print that sentence in an informational line
and then clear it.

SO BUG-1532'S FIX AS WRITTEN OVER-CORRECTS. You wrote: "the fix is a deletion: drop the
reason-text substring test against live drive specs." Dropping it makes pr_is_drive_owned
true for EVERY held PR, so `pr ship` refuses on all 24 markers — including the
supervised holds it exists to release. That converts a bypass into a deadlock: the
documented release path for a supervised hold stops working and there is no other
client-side release.

WHAT I WOULD ARGUE FOR INSTEAD — hold kind as first-class, which the substrate almost
has already:

  1. A marker records its KIND — supervised (a human decision is awaited) versus
     refusal (a reviewer rejected this commit) — rather than leaving it to reason prose.
     `aida merge-hold add` already takes --reason; this is one more field.
  2. pr ship RELEASES a supervised hold (unchanged, the BUG-1167 behaviour) and REFUSES
     a refusal hold, naming the verdict and the sha.
  3. A refusal hold is released only by a fresh verdict at the current head — which is
     BUG-1531 criterion 3 and BUG-1522 criterion 6's predicate again. Third consumer.
  4. Until kinds exist, the conservative read of an unkinded marker is REFUSAL, not
     supervised. That is your c9 shape — unknown is not clear — applied here.

MIGRATION NOTE, because criterion 4 is not free: all 24 current markers are unkinded, so
a conservative default refuses all of them and reintroduces the deadlock above until
they are kinded. The 24 are enumerable (aida merge-hold list) and their reason text is
already distinguishable by eye — mine and #2042/#2043 say REVIEWER HOLD, the supervised
ones say "is marked drive/unset". A one-time kinding pass is the smaller problem, and it
is the kind of thing that should be done by reading the list, not by a regex over prose.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not run pr ship in any form, including --dry-run. The sequence
above is read from pr_cmd.rs:1476, 1656 and 1793-1810 and their comments. I have not
verified empirically that the gate re-runs green fast enough for the bounded wait to
succeed — if it times out the merge fails, which would make this a deadlock rather than
a bypass in practice. That leg is unverified and I am not going to verify it by running
it on a held PR.
subject: aida pr ship releases merge-holds by design — both ADR-37 layers defeated on one command; the fix needs hold KIND, not deleting the guard's condition
